reviews.body:
Thanks for working on replacing the retired Anthropic default. I found several points that need to be addressed before moving forward.

4 approved findings: 3 inline, 1 in this review body.

### General

**BLOCKING** CI attempt 2 failed: [run #41202955529](https://github.com/microsoft/conductor/actions/runs/41202955529). The Python 3.13 Ubuntu and Windows jobs, and the Python 3.12 Ubuntu job, all failed ([3.13 Ubuntu](https://github.com/microsoft/conductor/actions/runs/41202955529/job/124884462214), [3.13 Windows](https://github.com/microsoft/conductor/actions/runs/41202955529/job/124884462215), [3.12 Ubuntu](https://github.com/microsoft/conductor/actions/runs/41202955529/job/124884462220)).

Resolve the CI failures on the reviewed commit, rerun the checks, and verify they pass before merging.

<!-- conductor-review:v2: -->
LGTM, thanks for replacing the retired default Anthropic model in the agent builder.

review_comments.body:
**BLOCKING** Schema-bearing agents that omit a model still fail before output recovery can run. They use `ToolOutput`, and the locked Pydantic AI 2.31.1 treats Sonnet 5.5 as supporting forced tools, so it sends `tool_choice={"type":"any"}`. Sonnet 5.5 rejects forced tool choice with HTTP 400 ([migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide#forced-tool-use)).

Choose an active default compatible with the current adapter, or configure Sonnet 5.5 with `anthropic_supports_forced_tool_choice=False` while retaining output validation and recovery. Add a mocked request-level regression test that checks the emitted `tool_choice`.

**BLOCKING** Sonnet 5.5 produces signed thinking blocks by default. During compaction, Conductor's chain can rewrite earlier tool results or remove older messages while leaving later thinking blocks intact; Pydantic AI then replays those blocks unchanged. For accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, Sonnet 5.5 rejects these altered conversation prefixes with HTTP 400 by default. A model-unspecified tool agent can therefore fail on its first request after compaction, even without an output schema. The compaction fail-open wrapper cannot recover because the rejection happens on the subsequent API request ([migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide#thinking-blocks)).

Use a compatible default until thinking-history handling is supported, or implement targeted prefix-mismatch recovery that strips the invalid block and subsequent thinking blocks before retrying once. Add a regression test for compaction of signed thinking history.

**BLOCKING** Three existing assertions in `tests/test_providers/test_claude.py` still expect the retired default: lines 134, 938, and 975. They cover default initialization and dialog turns with empty and populated history. Each constructs `ClaudeProvider` without a model override, so all three fail with the changed constructor.

Update those expectations to the intended replacement default while preserving the initialization and dialog-forwarding checks, then run both affected provider test files.

Fix confirmed. agent_builder.py:56 now selects claude-sonnet-4-6. ToolOutput validation and output retries remain at lines 251 and 661. tests/test_providers/test_pydantic_ai_agent_builder.py:117–171 adds a mocked HTTP request test asserting the default model, absent thinking configuration, and tool_choice={"type":"any"}.

Fix confirmed. tests/test_providers/test_claude.py:134, 938, and 975 now expect claude-sonnet-4-6. The surrounding initialization, prompt, and history assertions remain intact. Both affected files are included in the successful current-head CI suite; the Python 3.12 Ubuntu log reports 13,454 passed and 6 skipped.

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed review. Switched the default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`, which still accepts forced `tool_choice` and keeps the existing thinking-history handling, so the ToolOutput path and compaction behave as before. Updated the three `test_claude.py` expectations (default init and the two dialog turns) and added a mocked request-level test asserting the emitted `model`, no `thinking`, and `tool_choice={"type":"any"}`. Ruff and the provider test files pass locally.
